public_rationale: The claim is partly right. The 2024–2027 points are projections: the essay gives a 3–6 order-of-magnitude range with a 'best guess'. The effective-compute values also lean on what Aschenbrenner calls a naive back-of-the-envelope estimate of algorithmic gains. And OpenAI never disclosed GPT-4's training compute. But 'every data point is imaginary' goes too far. The essay says the 2019–2023 compute scaleup is traced from Epoch AI's public estimates of real training runs. Those are rough estimates of real quantities, not invented numbers. So the claim holds for the projected points and largely fails for the historical ones.
